title: Circular Estimate Method (CEM) for Estimating C. elegans Culture Densities
author: Josende, Nunes, et al.

steps.title: Prepare nematode stock and experimental suspensions
steps.instruction: Bleach gravid hermaphrodites with 50 mL of 0.8 M NaOH and 0.5 % NaClO, incubate eggs until hatching to obtain ~10 mL concentrated nematode suspension; stain this suspension with 5 % Rose Bengal, incubate 30 min at 80 °C, then dilute to a final volume of 30 mL in a 50 mL Falcon tube; aliquot 5 mL of this mixture into a 15 mL Falcon tube to serve as the Nematode Stock Suspension (NSS) for each experiment.

steps.title: Set up manual drop method replicates
steps.instruction: For each experimental sample, prime the pipette tip five times (cut the tip if worms are >500 µm) and, with the tip positioned in the middle of the ENS, dispense five 10 µL aliquots; count the worms in each drop, calculate the mean of the five counts, and extrapolate this mean to the total ENS volume following the adapted Solis and Petrascheck method.

steps.title: Collect aliquot from ENS for CEM
steps.instruction: Gently vortex the ENS, prime the pipette tip five times (cut tip if worms >500 µm), place the tip in the middle of the suspension, and pipette the desired aliquot (up to 500 µL) into a well of a 24‑well culture plate (TPP model 92,024).

steps.title: Homogenize sample in 24‑well plate
steps.instruction: If necessary, adjust the aliquot volume to ≤500 µL, then homogenize by pipetting the sample five times with the tip centered in the well; allow the worms to settle for 40–60 seconds before imaging.

steps.title: Capture and stitch well images
steps.instruction: Using a Leica S8APO microscope equipped with a Leica DFC295 camera, photograph the well; because the minimal zoom does not cover the entire well, acquire four overlapping images, include a reference scale bar in each, and stitch the images together to obtain a complete view of the well bottom.

steps.title: Calibrate ImageJ and draw counting circles
steps.instruction: Open the stitched image in ImageJ (Fiji); use the Straight tool to measure the length of the scale bar, set the pixel‑to‑mm relationship via ‘Set Scale’; draw an oval with a radius of 2.435 mm (diameter 4.87 mm) representing 1/10 of the well area (18.62 mm²); duplicate this circle three times to obtain four equally sized circles placed randomly on the image.

steps.title: Count worms in circles and extrapolate
steps.instruction: Select the Multi‑point tool and count only worms that lie entirely within each of the four circles; record the four counts, compute their average, and multiply the average by 10 to estimate the total number of worms in the whole well; further extrapolate this number to the entire ENS or NSS volume as required.

steps.title: Optional: Count remaining worms for validation
steps.instruction: For validation purposes, count all worms remaining in the well after the circle counts to obtain a real count (RC); use this RC as a correction factor for density discrepancies among different NSS samples.
